content.title: What You Need Before Installing JUnit 5
content.explanation:
**Understanding the JUnit 5 Architecture:**

Before installing, it's important to understand JUnit 5's modular architecture. Unlike JUnit 4, JUnit 5 is composed of several modules that work together.

**JUnit 5 Modules:**

```
JUnit 5
├── JUnit Platform (launches test frameworks)
│   ├── junit-platform-engine
│   └── junit-platform-launcher
├── JUnit Jupiter (new programming model)
│   ├── junit-jupiter-api (write tests)
│   └── junit-jupiter-engine (run tests)
└── JUnit Vintage (runs JUnit 3/4 tests)
    └── junit-vintage-engine
```

**What You Need:**

| Component | Minimum Version | Purpose |
|-----------|-----------------|---------|
| **Java Development Kit (JDK)** | Java 8 | JUnit 5 requires Java 8 or higher |
| **Build Tool (optional)** | Maven 3.6+ or Gradle 6.0+ | Dependency management (recommended) |
| **IDE (optional)** | Eclipse 2020+, IntelliJ 2020+, VS Code | Development environment |

**Checking Java Installation:**

```bash
java -version
```

Expected output (should be Java 8 or higher):
```
java version "11.0.18" 2023-01-17 LTS
Java(TM) SE Runtime Environment 18.9 (build 11.0.18+10-LTS)
Java HotSpot(TM) 64-Bit Server VM 18.9 (build 11.0.18+10-LTS, mixed mode)
```

**Installation Approaches:**

| Approach | Pros | Cons | Best For |
|----------|------|------|----------|
| **Maven** | Reproducible, dependency management, CI/CD ready | Requires Maven knowledge | Professional projects |
| **Gradle** | Fast, flexible, Groovy/Kotlin DSL | Learning curve | Modern Java projects |
| **IDE Only** | Quick start, simple setup | Not portable | Learning, prototypes |
| **Manual JAR** | No build tool needed | Version conflicts | Legacy projects |

**JUnit 5 Dependencies Explained:**

For most projects, you'll need:

- **junit-jupiter**: The main Jupiter aggregator artifact (includes API + Engine)
- **junit-platform-launcher**: For programmatic test execution (optional)
- **junit-vintage-engine**: Only if you have JUnit 4 tests to run

**Maven Dependency (simplified):**
```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
    <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
    <version>5.10.2</version>
    <scope>test</scope>
</dependency>
```

**Gradle Dependency (simplified):**
```groovy
testImplementation 'org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter:5.10.2'
```

content.title: Setting Up JUnit 5 in a Maven Project

steps.action: Create a new Maven project or use an existing one.
details:
If you don't have a Maven project, create one using the command line:
```bash
mvn archetype:generate -DgroupId=com.example \
  -DartifactId=junit-demo \
  -DarchetypeArtifactId=maven-archetype-quickstart \
  -DinteractiveMode=false
```
This creates a basic Java project structure:
```
junit-demo/
├── pom.xml
└── src/
    ├── main/
    │   └── java/
    │       └── com/example/App.java
    └── test/
        └── java/
            └── com/example/AppTest.java (JUnit 4 test)
```
steps.verification: Project structure is created with a valid `pom.xml` file.

steps.action: Add JUnit 5 dependencies to your Maven POM file.
details: Open the `pom.xml` file and replace the JUnit 4 dependency with JUnit 5:

```xml
<project>
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>
    <groupId>com.example</groupId>
    <artifactId>junit-demo</artifactId>
    <version>1.0-SNAPSHOT</version>

    <properties>
        <maven.compiler.source>11</maven.compiler.source>
        <maven.compiler.target>11</maven.compiler.target>
        <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>
        <junit.version>5.10.2</junit.version>
    </properties>

    <dependencies>
        <!-- JUnit 5 Jupiter API and Engine -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <version>${junit.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>

        <!-- Optional: Parameterized Tests -->
        <!-- Already included in junit-jupiter aggregator -->
        
        <!-- Optional: JUnit Vintage for JUnit 4 tests -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.vintage</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-vintage-engine</artifactId>
            <version>${junit.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.2.5</version>
                <configuration>
                    <!-- Enable JUnit Platform -->
                    <useModulePath>false</useModulePath>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>
```
steps.verification: Run `mvn dependency:tree` to verify JUnit 5 is downloaded.

steps.step: 3. Create a Simple JUnit 5 Test Class
steps.action: Create a basic JUnit 5 test to verify the setup.
steps.verification: File is created without compilation errors.

steps.action: Execute the tests using Maven commands.
details:
Open a terminal in your project directory and run:
```bash
# Run all tests
mvn clean test

# Run a specific test class
mvn test -Dtest=FirstTest

# Run a specific test method
mvn test -Dtest=FirstTest#testAddition

# Run with more detailed output
mvn test -X
```
Expected output should include:
```
[INFO] Running com.example.FirstTest
Before all tests
Before each test
After each test
Before each test
After each test
After all tests
[INFO] Tests run: 2, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0
```
steps.verification: Tests run successfully with 0 failures.

steps.action: Locate and view the generated test reports.
details:
After running tests, Maven generates reports in the `target/surefire-reports` directory:
```
target/surefire-reports/
├── TEST-com.example.FirstTest.xml          # JUnit XML report
├── com.example.FirstTest.txt                # Test output
└── TEST-com.example.FirstTest-output.txt    # System output
```
For HTML reports, you can use the surefire-report plugin:
```bash
mvn surefire-report:report
```
This generates `target/site/surefire-report.html` which you can open in a browser.
steps.verification: Reports are generated and can be viewed.

content.title: Complete Maven pom.xml with Advanced JUnit Configuration
content.scenario: A production-ready Maven project with comprehensive JUnit 5 setup.
content.outcome: A well-configured pom.xml with JUnit 5, parameterized tests, and reporting.
content.prevention: This configuration ensures consistent test execution across different environments.
content.details:
```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 
         http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <groupId>com.example</groupId>
    <artifactId>junit-advanced-demo</artifactId>
    <version>1.0-SNAPSHOT</version>

    <properties>
        <maven.compiler.source>11</maven.compiler.source>
        <maven.compiler.target>11</maven.compiler.target>
        <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>
        <junit.version>5.10.2</junit.version>
        <mockito.version>5.10.0</mockito.version>
        <surefire.version>3.2.5</surefire.version>
    </properties>

    <dependencies>
        <!-- JUnit 5 Jupiter API and Engine -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <version>${junit.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>

        <!-- Parameterized Tests (already in junit-jupiter, but explicit if needed) -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter-params</artifactId>
            <version>${junit.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>

        <!-- Mockito for mocking -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.mockito</groupId>
            <artifactId>mockito-core</artifactId>
            <version>${mockito.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.mockito</groupId>
            <artifactId>mockito-junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <version>${mockito.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>

        <!-- JUnit Vintage for JUnit 4 tests (if migrating) -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.vintage</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-vintage-engine</artifactId>
            <version>${junit.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>

        <!-- Hamcrest for additional assertions (optional) -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.hamcrest</groupId>
            <artifactId>hamcrest</artifactId>
            <version>2.2</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <!-- Compiler plugin -->
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.12.1</version>
                <configuration>
                    <source>${maven.compiler.source}</source>
                    <target>${maven.compiler.target}</target>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>

            <!-- Surefire plugin for running tests -->
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>${surefire.version}</version>
                <configuration>
                    <!-- Include/exclude test patterns -->
                    <includes>
                        <include>**/*Test.java</include>
                        <include>**/*Tests.java</include>
                        <include>**/*TestCase.java</include>
                    </includes>
                    <excludes>
                        <exclude>**/Abstract*Test.java</exclude>
                    </excludes>
                    
                    <!-- Parallel execution -->
                    <parallel>methods</parallel>
                    <threadCount>4</threadCount>
                    <perCoreThreadCount>true</perCoreThreadCount>
                    
                    <!-- Test failure handling -->
                    <testFailureIgnore>false</testFailureIgnore>
                    <skipTests>false</skipTests>
                    
                    <!-- System properties for tests -->
                    <systemPropertyVariables>
                        <environment>test</environment>
                        <test.timeout>5000</test.timeout>
                    </systemPropertyVariables>
                    
                    <!-- Detailed test output -->
                    <printSummary>true</printSummary>
                    <redirectTestOutputToFile>false</redirectTestOutputToFile>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>

            <!-- Surefire report plugin -->
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-surefire-report-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>${surefire.version}</version>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <phase>test</phase>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>report</goal>
                        </goals>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
            </plugin>

            <!-- JaCoCo for code coverage -->
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.jacoco</groupId>
                <artifactId>jacoco-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>0.8.11</version>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>prepare-agent</goal>
                        </goals>
                    </execution>
                    <execution>
                        <id>report</id>
                        <phase>test</phase>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>report</goal>
                        </goals>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>

    <profiles>
        <!-- Profile for fast unit tests -->
        <profile>
            <id>fast-tests</id>
            <build>
                <plugins>
                    <plugin>
                        <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                        <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                        <configuration>
                            <groups>unit & !slow</groups>
                        </configuration>
                    </plugin>
                </plugins>
            </build>
        </profile>

        <!-- Profile for integration tests -->
        <profile>
            <id>integration-tests</id>
            <build>
                <plugins>
                    <plugin>
                        <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                        <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                        <configuration>
                            <groups>integration</groups>
                        </configuration>
                    </plugin>
                </plugins>
            </build>
        </profile>
    </profiles>
</project>
```

**Usage Examples:**

```bash
# Run all tests
mvn clean test

# Run only unit tests (fast)
mvn test -Pfast-tests

# Run integration tests
mvn test -Pintegration-tests

# Run specific test method
mvn test -Dtest=CalculatorTest#testAddition

# Generate test report
mvn surefire-report:report

# Generate code coverage report
mvn jacoco:report
```

content.title: Setting Up JUnit 5 in a Gradle Project

steps.action: Create a new Gradle project or use an existing one.
details:
If you don't have a Gradle project, create one using the command line:
```bash
# Create a new Gradle project
mkdir junit-gradle-demo
cd junit-gradle-demo
gradle init --type java-application --test-framework junit-jupiter
```
Or create the basic structure manually:
```
junit-gradle-demo/
├── build.gradle
├── settings.gradle
└── src/
    ├── main/
    │   └── java/
    │       └── com/example/App.java
    └── test/
        └── java/
            └── com/example/AppTest.java
```
steps.verification: Project structure is created with a valid `build.gradle` file.

steps.action: Set up JUnit 5 dependencies in your Gradle build file.
details: Open `build.gradle` and configure it for JUnit 5:
steps.verification: Run `gradle dependencies` to verify JUnit 5 is downloaded.

steps.action: Create a basic test to verify the setup.
details: Update `src/test/java/com/example/AppTest.java`:
steps.verification: File is created without compilation errors.

steps.action: Execute the tests using Gradle commands.
details:
Open a terminal in your project directory and run:
```bash
# Run all tests
gradle clean test

# Run with more verbose output
gradle test --info

# Run a specific test class
gradle test --tests com.example.AppTest

# Run a specific test method
gradle test --tests com.example.AppTest.testAddition

# Generate test report
gradle test
# Report is in build/reports/tests/test/index.html

# Generate coverage report
gradle jacocoTestReport
# Report is in build/reports/jacoco/test/html/index.html
```
Expected output should include:
```
> Task :test

com.example.AppTest > testAddition() PASSED
com.example.AppTest > testException() PASSED
com.example.AppTest > testWithParameters(int) PASSED
...

BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 3s
```
steps.verification: Tests run successfully with 0 failures.

steps.action: Locate and view the generated test reports.
details:
After running tests, Gradle generates reports in the `build/reports` directory:
```
build/reports/tests/test/
├── index.html                    # Main test report
├── classes/
│   └── com.example.AppTest.html  # Class-specific report
├── css/                           # Report styling
├── js/                            # Report scripts
└── packages/                      # Package reports
```
Open `build/reports/tests/test/index.html` in a browser to see the detailed test report with:
- Overall test summary
- Pass/fail statistics
- Test execution times
- Failed test details
steps.verification: HTML report opens and shows passing tests.

content.title: Complete Gradle build.gradle with Advanced JUnit Configuration
content.scenario: A production-ready Gradle project with comprehensive JUnit 5 setup.
content.outcome: A well-configured build.gradle with parallel execution, reporting, and code coverage.
content.prevention: This configuration ensures consistent test execution across different environments.

steps.action: Check that your Eclipse has JUnit 5 support.
details:
Eclipse 2020-09 and later include JUnit 5 support out of the box.
To verify:
1. Go to **Help > About Eclipse**
2. Check that you have a recent version

If you need to install JUnit 5 support:
1. Go to **Help > Eclipse Marketplace**
2. Search for **'JUnit 5'**
3. Install **'JUnit 5 Support'** (if not already present)
steps.verification: JUnit 5 appears in the list of installed features.

steps.action: Create a Java project to use with JUnit.
details:
1. Go to **File > New > Java Project**
2. Enter a project name (e.g., `JUnitDemo`)
3. Select JRE version (Java 8 or higher)
4. Click **Finish**

**For Maven project:**
1. Go to **File > New > Other > Maven > Maven Project**
2. Select archetype `maven-archetype-quickstart`
3. Enter Group Id and Artifact Id
4. Click Finish
steps.verification: Project is created with proper structure.

steps.action: Add JUnit 5 library to your project.
details:
**For non-Maven/Gradle projects:**
1. Right-click on your project in Package Explorer
2. Select **Build Path > Configure Build Path**
3. Go to the **Libraries** tab
4. Click **Add Library**
5. Select **JUnit**
6. Choose **JUnit 5** as the version
7. Click **Finish**
8. Click **Apply and Close**

**For Maven projects:**
1. Add JUnit 5 dependency to `pom.xml` (as shown earlier)
2. Right-click project > **Maven > Update Project** (Alt+F5)

**For Gradle projects:**
1. Add JUnit 5 dependency to `build.gradle`
2. Right-click project > **Gradle > Refresh Gradle Project**
steps.verification: JUnit 5 appears in your project's referenced libraries.

steps.action: Create your first JUnit 5 test class in Eclipse.
steps.verification: Test class is created without compilation errors.

steps.action: Execute JUnit tests using different methods.
details:
**Method 1: Run as JUnit Test**
- Right-click on the test class → **Run As > JUnit Test**
- Right-click on a specific test method → **Run As > JUnit Test**
- Right-click on a package → **Run As > JUnit Test** (runs all tests in package)

**Method 2: Use toolbar**
- Click the **Run** button dropdown → **Run As > JUnit Test**

**Method 3: Keyboard shortcuts**
- `Alt+Shift+X, T` (Run as JUnit Test)
- `Ctrl+F11` (Rerun last test)

**View Results:**
- The **JUnit** view opens automatically
- Green bar indicates all tests passed
- Red bar indicates failures
- Double-click on a failure to see the stack trace
- Click on a test method to see execution time
steps.verification: Tests run successfully and JUnit view shows passing results.

steps.action: Ensure your IntelliJ IDEA supports JUnit 5.
details:
IntelliJ IDEA 2017.3 and later have built-in JUnit 5 support.
To verify:
1. Go to **File > Settings** (Windows/Linux) or **IntelliJ IDEA > Preferences** (macOS)
2. Navigate to **Build, Execution, Deployment > Build Tools > Maven** (or Gradle)
3. Ensure JUnit 5 is enabled

JUnit 5 plugin is bundled and enabled by default in recent versions.
steps.verification: JUnit 5 support is available.

steps.action: Create a Java project with JUnit 5 support.
details:
1. Go to **File > New > Project**
2. Select **Java** from the left panel
3. Choose JDK (Java 8 or higher)
4. Click **Next**
5. Check **Create project from template** (optional)
6. Click **Next**
7. Enter project name and location
8. Click **Finish**

**For Maven project:**
1. Select **Maven** from left panel
2. Check **Create from archetype**
3. Select `maven-archetype-quickstart`
4. Click Next, enter GroupId and ArtifactId
5. Click Finish
6. Add JUnit 5 dependency to `pom.xml`

**For Gradle project:**
1. Select **Gradle** from left panel
2. Choose Java as language
3. Enter GroupId and ArtifactId
4. Click Finish
5. Add JUnit 5 dependency to `build.gradle`
steps.verification: Project is created with proper structure.

steps.action: Add JUnit 5 to your project dependencies.
details:
**For Maven:** Add to `pom.xml`:
```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
    <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
    <version>5.10.2</version>
    <scope>test</scope>
</dependency>
```
**For Gradle:** Add to `build.gradle`:
```groovy
testImplementation 'org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter:5.10.2'
```
**For simple Java project:**
1. Go to **File > Project Structure** (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+S)
2. Select **Libraries**
3. Click **+ > From Maven**
4. Search for `org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter`
5. Select version and click **OK**
steps.verification: JUnit 5 appears in external libraries.

steps.action: Create your first JUnit 5 test class in IntelliJ.
steps.verification: Test class is created without compilation errors.

steps.action: Execute JUnit tests using different methods.
details:
**Method 1: Run gutter icons**
- Click the green triangle ▶️ next to the class declaration to run all tests in the class
- Click the green triangle ▶️ next to a test method to run only that method

**Method 2: Run context menu**
- Right-click on the test class → **Run 'CalculatorTest'**
- Right-click on a test method → **Run 'testMethod'**
- Right-click on a package → **Run 'Tests in...'**

**Method 3: Keyboard shortcuts**
- `Ctrl+Shift+F10` (Run context test)
- `Shift+F10` (Rerun last test)

**View Results:**
- The **Run** tool window opens
- Green checkmarks for passed tests
- Red X for failed tests
- Click on a test to see stack trace
- Execution time shown for each test
steps.verification: Tests run successfully and results appear in Run window.

steps.action: Install VS Code extensions for Java and JUnit support.

Open VS Code and go to the Extensions view (`Ctrl+Shift+X`).
Install the following extensions:
1. **Extension Pack for Java** (by Microsoft) - includes Java language support, debugger, test runner, Maven/Gradle support
2. **Java Test Runner** (already included in the pack)

Alternatively, you can install these individually:
- Language Support for Java™ by Red Hat
- Debugger for Java
- Test Runner for Java
- Maven for Java
- Project Manager for Java
steps.verification: Extensions are installed and enabled.

steps.action: Configure JUnit 5 in your build file.
details:
**For Maven projects:**
1. Open `pom.xml`
2. Add JUnit 5 dependency:
```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
    <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
    <version>5.10.2</version>
    <scope>test</scope>
</dependency>
```
3. Save the file - VS Code automatically downloads dependencies

**For Gradle projects:**
1. Open `build.gradle`
2. Add JUnit 5 dependency:
```groovy
dependencies {
    testImplementation 'org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter:5.10.2'
}

test {
    useJUnitPlatform()
}
```
3. Save the file - VS Code automatically refreshes
steps.verification: JUnit 5 appears in Java Projects view under 'Referenced Libraries'.

steps.action: Create a JUnit 5 test class in VS Code.
steps.verification: Test class is created without compilation errors.

steps.action: Execute JUnit tests using VS Code's test runner.
details:
**Method 1: Using Test Explorer**
1. Click the **Beaker** icon in the left sidebar (Testing view)
2. You'll see all test classes and methods
3. Click the **Play** button next to a test to run it
4. Click the **Play** button at the top to run all tests

**Method 2: Using CodeLens**
- Look for **'Run Test'** links above test classes and methods in the editor
- Click **'Run Test'** to execute that specific test

**Method 3: Using Command Palette**
1. `Ctrl+Shift+P` → **Java: Run Tests**

**View Results:**
- Test results appear in the Testing view
- Green checkmarks for passed tests
- Red X for failed tests
- Click on a test to see stack trace and output
- Execution time shown for each test
steps.verification: Tests run successfully and results appear in Testing view.

steps.action: Run JUnit tests from command line to verify build tool integration.
details:
**For Maven projects:**
```bash
cd your-project-directory
```

content.title: Common Installation Issues and Solutions
content.scenario: You've followed the setup steps but tests aren't running correctly.
content.outcome: Quick resolution of common JUnit installation problems.
content.prevention: Knowing these solutions saves hours of frustration.
content.details:
**Issue 1: JUnit annotations not recognized**

- **Symptom:** `@Test` shows red underline, imports not working
- **Solution:**
    - **Maven/Gradle:** Run `mvn clean install` or `gradle clean build` to download dependencies
    - **Eclipse:** Right-click project > Maven > Update Project (Alt+F5)
    - **IntelliJ:** Click the Maven refresh button in the tool window
    - **VS Code:** Check that Java extensions are properly installed

**Issue 2: Tests not showing in IDE run configurations**

- **Symptom:** Right-click doesn't show "Run as JUnit Test" option
- **Solution:**
    - **Eclipse:** Ensure project is configured as Java project with JUnit on classpath
    - **IntelliJ:** File > Settings > Build Tools > ensure JUnit is enabled
    - **VS Code:** Check that Test Runner extension is installed

**Issue 3: No tests found or executed**

- **Symptom:** "No tests found" message when running tests
- **Solution:**
    - **Maven:** Check surefire plugin configuration in pom.xml
    - **Gradle:** Ensure `useJUnitPlatform()` is configured
    - **Method visibility:** JUnit 5 test methods must be package-private or public
    - **Naming:** Test classes must not be abstract

**Issue 4: JUnit 4 vs JUnit 5 conflicts**

- **Symptom:** Both JUnit 4 and JUnit 5 dependencies present
- **Solution:**
    - Remove JUnit 4 dependencies if you're using JUnit 5
    - If you need both, ensure vintage engine is included for JUnit 4 tests
    - Check dependency tree: `mvn dependency:tree`

**Issue 5: Parameterized tests not working**

- **Symptom:** `@ParameterizedTest` annotation not recognized
- **Solution:**
    - Ensure `junit-jupiter-params` is in dependencies (or use `junit-jupiter` aggregator)
    - Check import statements

**Issue 6: java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError for JUnit classes**

- **Symptom:** Runtime errors about missing JUnit classes
- **Solution:**
    - Check that JUnit is in the correct scope (`test` scope for Maven/Gradle)
    - Ensure JUnit JARs are in the classpath when running tests
    - For IDE, check project structure and dependencies

**Issue 7: Tests run but all are skipped**

- **Symptom:** Tests show as SKIPPED with no execution
- **Solution:**
    - Check for `@Disabled` annotation
    - Check assumptions that might be failing (`assumeTrue`)
    - Check test method visibility

**Issue 8: Outdated JUnit version warnings**

- **Symptom:** Warning about using older JUnit version
- **Solution:**
    - Update to latest JUnit 5 version
    - Check for transitive dependencies pulling older versions
    - Use dependency management to enforce versions

**Issue 9: IntelliJ doesn't recognize test class**

- **Symptom:** Test class icon not showing as test
- **Solution:**
    - Mark directory as test sources root (right-click > Mark Directory as > Test Sources Root)
    - File > Project Structure > Modules > mark test folders
    - Invalidate caches: File > Invalidate Caches and Restart

**Issue 10: VS Code test runner not showing tests**

- **Symptom:** Testing view is empty
- **Solution:**
    - Reload VS Code window
    - Check Java extension output for errors
    - Ensure project is properly loaded by Java language server
    - Try "Java: Clean Java Language Server Workspace" command

**Issue 11: Classpath issues with multiple modules**

- **Symptom:** Tests can't find classes from other modules
- **Solution:**
    - **Maven:** Ensure correct dependencies between modules
    - **Gradle:** Configure project dependencies properly
    - **IDE:** Check module dependencies in project structure

**Issue 12: Slow test execution**

- **Symptom:** Tests take too long to run
- **Solution:**
    - Enable parallel execution
    - Use `@TestInstance(Lifecycle.PER_CLASS)` to reduce instance creation
    - Profile and optimize slow tests
    - Use `@Timeout` to identify hanging tests

content.title: Grouping Tests for Efficient Execution
content.explanation:
**Beyond Individual Test Classes**

A test suite is a collection of test cases that can be run together as a group. Test suites allow you to organize tests logically and execute them efficiently.

**Why Use Test Suites?**

| Reason | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Organization** | Group related tests together (by feature, module, type) |
| **Selective Execution** | Run specific groups of tests (smoke, regression, integration) |
| **Efficiency** | Run multiple test classes with one command |
| **CI/CD Integration** | Different suites for different pipeline stages |
| **Reporting** | Aggregated results for related tests |
| **Maintainability** | Easy to add/remove tests from logical groups |

**JUnit 4 vs JUnit 5 Test Suites:**

| JUnit 4 | JUnit 5 |
|---------|---------|
| `@RunWith(Suite.class)` | `@Suite` |
| `@Suite.SuiteClasses({...})` | `@SelectClasses({...})` |
| Package scanning via libraries | `@SelectPackages` |
| Limited filtering | `@IncludeTags`, `@ExcludeTags` |

**Basic JUnit 5 Test Suite:**

```java
import org.junit.platform.suite.api.SelectPackages;
import org.junit.platform.suite.api.Suite;

@Suite
@SelectPackages("com.example.tests")
public class AllTestsSuite {
    // Empty class - just for configuration
}
```

**Test Suite Architecture:**

```
Master Test Suite
├── Smoke Test Suite
│   ├── LoginTest
│   ├── CheckoutTest
│   └── PaymentTest
├── Regression Test Suite
│   ├── Unit Tests
│   │   ├── CalculatorTest
│   │   └── StringUtilsTest
│   ├── Integration Tests
│   │   ├── DatabaseTest
│   │   └── ApiTest
│   └── UI Tests
│       ├── LoginUITest
│       └── CheckoutUITest
└── Performance Test Suite
    ├── LoadTest
    └── StressTest
```

```yaml
# Unit tests (run on every commit)
```

steps.action: Add rules to control pipeline flow.
details:
```yaml
# Define a job that checks test results
check-results:
  stage: report
  script:
    - |
      # Check for test failures
      if grep -q '<failure' target/surefire-reports/*.xml; then
        echo "❌ Tests failed!"
        
        # Check if critical tests failed
        if grep -q 'critical.*<failure' target/surefire-reports/*.xml; then
          echo "❌ Critical tests failed - blocking deployment"
          exit 1
        else
          echo "⚠️ Non-critical tests failed - continuing with warning"
        fi
      fi
      
      # Calculate pass rate
      TOTAL=$(grep -o 'tests="[0-9]*"' target/surefire-reports/*.xml | awk -F'"' '{sum+=$2} END {print sum}')
      FAILED=$(grep -o 'failures="[0-9]*"' target/surefire-reports/*.xml | awk -F'"' '{sum+=$2} END {print sum}')
      
      if [ $TOTAL -gt 0 ]; then
        PASS_RATE=$(( (TOTAL - FAILED) * 100 / TOTAL ))
        echo "Pass rate: $PASS_RATE%"
        
        if [ $PASS_RATE -lt 95 ]; then
          echo "❌ Pass rate below 95%"
          exit 1
        fi
      fi
      
      echo "✅ Quality gate passed"
  needs:
    - unit-tests
    - integration-tests
    - regression-tests
  only:
    - main

deploy-staging:
  stage: deploy
  script:
    - echo "Deploying to staging..."
    - ./deploy.sh staging
  needs:
    - check-results
  only:
    - main
```
steps.verification: Pipeline stops if quality gate conditions are not met.

content.details:
**.gitlab-ci.yml:**

```yaml
# Complete GitLab CI pipeline for JUnit
stages:
  - build
  - unit-test
  - integration-test
  - report
  - deploy

variables:
  MAVEN_OPTS: "-Dmaven.repo.local=$CI_PROJECT_DIR/.m2/repository"
  MAVEN_CLI_OPTS: "--batch-mode --errors --fail-at-end --show-version"
  TEST_ENV: "staging"

cache:
  key: "${CI_COMMIT_REF_SLUG}"
  paths:
    - .m2/repository/

before_script:
  - echo "Starting pipeline for branch $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH"
  - java -version
  - mvn -version

# Build job
build:
  stage: build
  script:
    - mvn $MAVEN_CLI_OPTS compile
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - target/classes/
    expire_in: 1 hour

# Unit tests (fast, run on all commits)
unit-test:
  stage: unit-test
  script:
    - mvn $MAVEN_CLI_OPTS test -Dgroups=unit
  artifacts:
    when: always
    paths:
      - target/surefire-reports/
    reports:
      junit: target/surefire-reports/*.xml
    expire_in: 1 week

# Integration tests (run on main branch and MRs)
integration-test:
  stage: integration-test
  script:
    - mvn $MAVEN_CLI_OPTS test -Dgroups=integration -Denvironment=$TEST_ENV
  artifacts:
    when: always
    paths:
      - target/surefire-reports/
    reports:
      junit: target/surefire-reports/*.xml
  only:
    - main
    - merge_requests

# Parallel test execution for performance tests
parallel-test:
  stage: integration-test
  parallel: 3
  script:
    - mvn $MAVEN_CLI_OPTS test -Dgroups=performance -Dthread=$CI_NODE_INDEX
  artifacts:
    when: always
    paths:
      - target/surefire-reports/
    reports:
      junit: target/surefire-reports/*.xml
  only:
    - schedules

# Generate HTML report
html-report:
  stage: report
  script:
    - mvn surefire-report:report
    - mkdir -p public
    - cp -r target/site/* public/
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - public
  only:
    - main

# Quality gate
quality-gate:
  stage: report
  script:
    - |
      echo "Checking test results..."
      
      # Count failures
      FAILURES=$(grep -r 'failures="[1-9]' target/surefire-reports/ | wc -l)
      ERRORS=$(grep -r 'errors="[1-9]' target/surefire-reports/ | wc -l)
      
      echo "Failures: $FAILURES, Errors: $ERRORS"
      
      if [ $FAILURES -gt 0 ] || [ $ERRORS -gt 0 ]; then
        echo "❌ Tests failed!"
        
        # Check for critical failures
        if grep -q '@Tag.*critical.*' src/test/java/ && grep -q '<failure' target/surefire-reports/TEST-*critical*.xml; then
          echo "❌ Critical tests failed - blocking deployment"
          exit 1
        fi
      fi
      
      echo "✅ Quality gate passed"
  needs:
    - unit-test
    - integration-test
  only:
    - main

# Deploy to staging
deploy-staging:
  stage: deploy
  script:
    - echo "Deploying to staging environment..."
    - ./deploy.sh staging $CI_COMMIT_SHA
  environment:
    name: staging
    url: https://staging.example.com
  only:
    - main
  needs:
    - quality-gate

# Deploy to production (manual approval)
deploy-production:
  stage: deploy
  script:
    - echo "Deploying to production..."
    - ./deploy.sh production $CI_COMMIT_SHA
  environment:
    name: production
    url: https://example.com
  only:
    - tags
  when: manual
  needs:
    - quality-gate
```

steps.action: Create `.github/workflows/junit-tests.yml`.
details:
```yaml
name: JUnit Tests

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, develop ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 2 * * *'  # Run daily at 2 AM
  workflow_dispatch:  # Manual trigger

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        java-version: [11, 17, 21]
        test-type: [unit, integration]
      fail-fast: false  # Don't cancel all if one fails
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v3
      
      - name: Set up JDK ${{ matrix.java-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-java@v3
        with:
          java-version: ${{ matrix.java-version }}
          distribution: 'temurin'
          cache: maven
      
      - name: Run ${{ matrix.test-type }} tests
        run: |
          mvn clean test -Dgroups=${{ matrix.test-type }} \
            -Denvironment=${{ secrets.TEST_ENV }}
      
      - name: Upload test results
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        if: always()  # Upload even if tests fail
        with:
          name: ${{ matrix.test-type }}-results-jdk${{ matrix.java-version }}
          path: target/surefire-reports/
      
      - name: Publish Test Report
        uses: mikepenz/action-junit-report@v3
        if: always()
        with:
          report_paths: target/surefire-reports/*.xml
          check_name: ${{ matrix.test-type }} Test Report (JDK ${{ matrix.java-version }})
```

content.title: Complete GitHub Actions Workflow for JUnit
content.scenario: A comprehensive GitHub Actions workflow for a Java application with JUnit tests.
content.outcome: A fully automated CI/CD pipeline with matrix testing, reporting, and deployment.
content.prevention: Automated testing ensures code quality across multiple JDKs and OS platforms.
content.details:
**.github/workflows/ci.yml:**

```yaml
name: Java CI with JUnit

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop, release/*]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 */6 * * *'  # Every 6 hours
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      environment:
        description: 'Test environment'
        required: true
        default: 'staging'
        type: choice
        options:
          - dev
          - staging
          - production

env:
  MAVEN_OPTS: -Dmaven.repo.local=${{ github.workspace }}/.m2/repository
  TEST_ENV: ${{ github.event.inputs.environment || 'staging' }}

jobs:
  # Build job
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Set up JDK 11
        uses: actions/setup-java@v3
        with:
          java-version: '11'
          distribution: 'temurin'
          cache: maven
      - name: Build with Maven
        run: mvn clean compile
      - name: Upload build artifacts
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        with:
          name: build-artifacts
          path: target/classes/

  # Unit tests (run on all platforms)
  unit-tests:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest, macos-latest]
        java-version: [11, 17, 21]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Set up JDK ${{ matrix.java-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-java@v3
        with:
          java-version: ${{ matrix.java-version }}
          distribution: 'temurin'
          cache: maven
      - name: Run unit tests
        run: mvn test -Dgroups=unit
      - name: Upload test results
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        if: always()
        with:
          name: unit-results-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.java-version }}
          path: target/surefire-reports/

  # Integration tests (run on main branch only)
  integration-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Set up JDK 11
        uses: actions/setup-java@v3
        with:
          java-version: '11'
          distribution: 'temurin'
          cache: maven
      - name: Run integration tests
        run: mvn test -Dgroups=integration -Denvironment=${{ env.TEST_ENV }}
      - name: Upload test results
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-results
          path: target/surefire-reports/

  # Quality gate
  quality-gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [unit-tests, integration-tests]
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Download all test results
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: artifacts/
      
      - name: Check quality gates
        run: |
          # Install required tools
          sudo apt-get install -y xmlstarlet
          
          FAILED=0
          
          # Check each test result file
          for file in $(find artifacts -name "TEST-*.xml"); do
            echo "Checking $file"
            
            # Get test counts
            TOTAL=$(xmlstarlet sel -t -v "sum(//testsuite/@tests)" $file)
            FAILURES=$(xmlstarlet sel -t -v "sum(//testsuite/@failures)" $file)
            ERRORS=$(xmlstarlet sel -t -v "sum(//testsuite/@errors)" $file)
            
            echo "  Tests: $TOTAL, Failures: $FAILURES, Errors: $ERRORS"
            
            if [ $FAILURES -gt 0 ] || [ $ERRORS -gt 0 ]; then
              # Check if this is a critical test
              if grep -q '@Tag.*critical.*' $file; then
                echo "❌ Critical test failure in $file"
                FAILED=1
              else
                echo "⚠️ Non-critical test failure in $file"
              fi
            fi
          done
          
          exit $FAILED

  # Deploy based on results
  deploy:
    needs: quality-gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: success() && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    environment: ${{ env.TEST_ENV }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Deploy to ${{ env.TEST_ENV }}
        run: |
          echo "Deploying to ${{ env.TEST_ENV }}..."
          ./deploy.sh ${{ env.TEST_ENV }}

  # Notify on completion
  notify:
    needs: [unit-tests, integration-tests, quality-gate]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Send Slack notification
        uses: 8398a7/action-slack@v3
        with:
          status: ${{ job.status }}
          fields: repo,message,commit,author,workflow
          text: |
            ${{ job.status == 'success' && '✅' || '❌' }} Test run completed
            Quality Gate: ${{ needs.quality-gate.result }}
        env:
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK }}
```

content.title: Making Test Results Visible and Actionable
content.explanation:
**Beyond JUnit XML: Rich Test Reporting** While JUnit XML reports are essential for CI tools, rich HTML reports provide better visibility for teams. **1. Maven Surefire Reports** ```xml org.apache.maven.plugins maven-surefire-report-plugin 3.2.5 test report ``` ```bash # Generate HTML report mvn surefire-report:report # Report location: target/site/surefire-report.html ``` **2. JaCoCo Code Coverage Reports** ```xml org.jacoco jacoco-maven-plugin 0.8.11 prepare-agent report test report ``` ```bash # Generate coverage report mvn jacoco:report # Report location: target/site/jacoco/index.html ``` **3. Custom HTML Report Generation** ```java import java.io.*; import java.nio.file.*; import javax.xml.parsers.*; import org.w3c.dom.*; public class TestReportGenerator { public static void generateHtmlReport(String reportDir) throws Exception { Path htmlPath = Paths.get(reportDir, "custom-report.html"); try (PrintWriter writer = new PrintWriter(Files.newBufferedWriter(htmlPath))) { writer.println(""); writer.println(""); writer.println("Test Report"); writer.println(""); writer.println("

Test Execution Report

"); // Parse JUnit XML files DocumentBuilderFactory factory = DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance(); DocumentBuilder builder = factory.newDocumentBuilder(); Files.walk(Paths.get(reportDir)) .filter(p -> p.toString().endsWith(".xml")) .forEach(xmlFile -> { try { Document doc = builder.parse(xmlFile.toFile()); NodeList testsuites = doc.getElementsByTagName("testsuite"); for (int i = 0; i < testsuites.getLength(); i++) { Element suite = (Element) testsuites.item(i); String name = suite.getAttribute("name"); int tests = Integer.parseInt(suite.getAttribute("tests")); int failures = Integer.parseInt(suite.getAttribute("failures")); int errors = Integer.parseInt(suite.getAttribute("errors")); int skipped = Integer.parseInt(suite.getAttribute("skipped")); writer.println("

" + name + "

"); writer.println(""); writer.println(""); writer.println(""); writer.println(""); writer.println(""); writer.println(""); writer.println("
Total" + tests + "
Passed" + (tests - failures - errors - skipped) + "
Failed" + failures + "
Errors" + errors + "
Skipped" + skipped + "
"); } } catch (Exception e) { e.printStackTrace(); } }); writer.println(""); } } } ``` **4. CI/CD Report Integration** **Jenkins:** ```groovy post { always { // Publish JUnit results junit 'target/surefire-reports/*.xml' // Publish HTML report publishHTML([ reportDir: 'target/site', reportFiles: 'surefire-report.html', reportName: 'Test Report' ]) // Publish coverage report publishHTML([ reportDir: 'target/site/jacoco', reportFiles: 'index.html', reportName: 'Code Coverage' ]) } } ``` **GitLab CI:** ```yaml test: stage: test script: - mvn test surefire-report:report jacoco:report artifacts: paths: - target/surefire-reports/ - target/site/ reports: junit: target/surefire-reports/*.xml ``` **GitHub Actions:** ```yaml - name: Generate reports run: mvn surefire-report:report jacoco:report - name: Upload reports uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3 with: name: test-reports path: | target/site/ target/surefire-reports/ ``` **5. Test Result Trends** ```python # analyze_trends.py import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET import json from datetime import datetime class TestTrendAnalyzer: def __init__(self): self.trends = { 'dates': [], 'totals': [], 'failures': [], 'passRates': [] } def add_build_results(self, xml_file): tree = ET.parse(xml_file) root = tree.getroot() total = int(root.get('tests', 0)) failures = int(root.get('failures', 0)) + int(root.get('errors', 0)) pass_rate = ((total - failures) / total * 100) if total > 0 else 0 self.trends['dates'].append(datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d')) self.trends['totals'].append(total) self.trends['failures'].append(failures) self.trends['passRates'].append(pass_rate) def generate_report(self): import matplotlib.pyplot as plt plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6)) plt.subplot(1, 2, 1) plt.plot(self.trends['dates'], self.trends['passRates'], 'g-o') plt.title('Pass Rate Trend') plt.ylabel('Pass Rate (%)') plt.xticks(rotation=45) plt.subplot(1, 2, 2) plt.bar(self.trends['dates'], self.trends['failures'], color='red') plt.title('Failure Trend') plt.ylabel('Number of Failures') plt.xticks(rotation=45) plt.tight_layout() plt.savefig('trend-report.png') ``` **6. Best Practices for CI/CD Reporting** | Practice | Implementation | Benefit | |----------|----------------|---------| | **Always archive reports** | Store as artifacts | Historical analysis | | **Use JUnit XML format** | Standard CI integration | Works with all tools | | **Generate HTML reports** | Developer-friendly | Easy debugging | | **Include screenshots** | For UI tests | Visual debugging | | **Track trends** | Historical data | Identify regression | | **Set thresholds** | Quality gates | Prevent degradation | | **Notify on failures** | Slack/email alerts | Immediate awareness | | **Link to code** | Include commit info | Traceability | | **Add metadata** | Build number, date | Context | | **Make reports accessible** | Publish to web | Share with team | **7. Complete Reporting Pipeline Example** ```yaml # .gitlab-ci.yml with comprehensive reporting stages: - test - report - pages test: stage: test script: - mvn clean test jacoco:report surefire-report:report artifacts: paths: - target/surefire-reports/ - target/site/ reports: junit: target/surefire-reports/*.xml generate-report: stage: report script: # Generate trend analysis - python scripts/analyze_tests.py # Generate coverage badge - python scripts/generate_badge.py # Create combined report - mkdir -p public - cp -r target/site/* public/ - cp trend-report.png public/ - cp badge.svg public/ artifacts: paths: - public/ pages: stage: pages script: - echo "Publishing reports to GitLab Pages" artifacts: paths: - public/ only: - main ```
